name: Sikagard-62 T
paste:
SIKAGARD®-62 T: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sikagard®-62 T, April 2023, Version 01.02 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/7/sikagard-62-t.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sikagard®-62 T where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.02).
1.2 Product description. Sikagard®-62 T is a trowelable/sprayable ultra high build lining for harsh environments.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. Sikagard®-62 T is used as a protective lining for:
    - Chemical bunds area
    - Waste Water Treatment and Holding Facilities
    - Storm Water Pits
    - Drinking Water Facilities
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.7.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sikagard®-62 T
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: Ultra high build chemically resistant coating / lining
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals, certificates and standards stated by the manufacturer. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (April 2023, Version 01.02) has no approvals, certificates or standards section.
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - EN 12944-4: referred to in instructions or limitations. Where: Application Instructions > Steel Surface (p.3).
    - EN 14879: referred to in instructions or limitations. Where: Application Instructions > Steel Surface (p.3).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Protective and decorative.
    - Excellent chemical resistance.
    - Easy for cleaning and graffiti removal.
    - High abrasion resistance.
    - Excellent adhesion to most building materials.
    - Can be built up to 5mm per pass.
    - Approved for use with potable water.
    - Can be spray applied.
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Epoxy resin
    - Appearance and colour: Grey
    - Density: Mixed resin approx. 1.28 kg/l; Density values determined at +23 °C
2.6 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Compressive strength: Approx. 50 MPa at 7 days
    - Tensile strength in flexure: Approx. 50 MPa at 7 days
    - Tensile strength: Approx. 25 MPa at 7 days
    - Modulus of elasticity in tension: Approx. 30-40 x10² MPa at 7 days
2.7 Tensile adhesion strength.
    | Dry concrete | 3.5 MPa * |
    | Sandblasted steel | 25 MPa |
    | Aluminium | 16 MPa |
    * failure in concrete
2.8 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Shelf life: 24 months from date of production
    - Storage conditions: The packaging must be stored properly in original, unopened and undamaged sealed packaging, in dry conditions at temperatures between +5 °C and +30 °C. Protected from direct sunlight.
2.9 Packaging.
    | Part A | 18 kg |
    | Part B | 6 kg |

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.02) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality. The substrate must be sound, clean, dry, free from contaminants such as dirt, grease, oil, old coatings, release agents, laitance and other adhesion preventing or influencing substances. On high absorbent, non-sound, contaminated, not cement based substrates precautions have to be taken and a suitable primer has to be used.
3.3 Substrate preparation - Concrete Substrates. Concrete substrate must be prepared mechanically to achieve an open textured surface. Weak areas in the substrate must be removed and surface defects such as blowholes and voids must be fully exposed. All dust, loose and friable material must be completely removed from all surfaces before application of the product, preferably by brush and/or vacuum. Open voids and blowholes need to be closed with a suitable Sika® pore filling mortar. The roughness of the substrate needs to be levelled with a suitable Sika® rendering and levelling mortar.
3.4 Substrate preparation - Steel Surface. Steel surface must be prepared mechanically using abrasive blast cleaning. The level SSPC-SP 10 “near white metal blast cleaned” or level Sa 2 ½ according to ISO EN 12944-4 has to be achieved. Welds and joints have to be prepared according to EN 14879, part 1. After blast cleaning remove all dust dirt and blasting material. In order to maintain the surface conditions after blast cleaning air-conditioning is recommended.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.02) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Consumption: Theoretical coverage of 3.6m² at 5mm thickness per 24 kg kit, depending on substrate profile and texture, waste factor etc.
    - Pot Life: Approx. 30 mins. at +20oC
4.3 Curing time.
    | 30oC | 20oC | 10oC |
    | Overcoating | 5 hrs | 10 hrs | 18 hrs |
    | Walkable | 8 hrs | 17 hrs | 24 hrs |
    | Full chemical res- | 5-9 days | 12 days | 15 days |
    | istance |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    Note: Sikagard®-62 T reaches 90% of its full cure at 20 oC in 4 days.
4.4 Mixing. Prior to mixing stir part A mechanically. When all of part B has been added to part A mix continuously for 3 minutes until a uniform mix has been achieved. Use a low speed electrical stirrer (300–400 rpm) to avoid air entrapment. To ensure proper mixing pour material into a clean container and stir again.
4.5 Application. Apply by brush, roller or airless spray.
4.6 Cleaning of equipment. Clean all tools with Thinner C immediately after use. Hardened and/or cured material can only be removed mechanically.
4.7 Limitations and important considerations.
    - Do not dilute the product as this will effect in-service performance. Thinner or solvents must not be used.
    - For application in damp conditions please Consult out Technical Department for further information.
    - Do not part mi containers.
    - Do not mix and apply product that has a temperature of greater than 30oC. If applying at higher 30oC, as soon as the Sikagard®-62 T is mixed transfer the container into an esky containing ice to just below the rim of the container, then apply the Sikagard®-62 T from the open container in the esky.
    - The temperature at which the Sikagard®-62 T is stored during the 24 hours before it is mixed will govern its potlife when mixed.
    - If the temperature of a porous substrate (which includes the avast majority of concrete) is rising i.e. is in direct sunlight prior to late afternoon, the air in the pores and cracks is expanding and if a wet coating is placed over such a substrate the expanding air will blow bubbles in the coating and pervent the liquid coating penetrating the substrate pores and cracks etc. Prior to the coating reaching the gel phase the bubbles will burst and leave "pinholes in coating, whereas during the gel phase, the bubbles will be "frozen" into the cured coating. These bubbles will be a weak point in the coating as their wall thickness will be less than the applied film thickness on the substrate.
    - To avoid unslightly water spotting do not apply Sikagard®-62 T when ambient temperature will reach "dew point" before the coating has cured.
    - Similarly do not allow water to contact Sikagard®-62 T that is not even seven (7) days old at 20oC or older at lower temperatures since it will mark the coating.
    - Do not apply Sikagard®-62 T to cementitious mortars that are modified with acrylic, acrylic co-polymer, EVA or PVA polymers (eg. SikaTops or Sika Mono-tops) because under certain environment conditions hardened mortar or render may swell slightly and cracks the rigid epoxy coating.
    - Light colours will yellow with exposure to sunlight or UV radiation.
    - Please consult our Technical Department for further information.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Temperature resistance. Permanent maximum: dry 70oC & wet 60oC
5.3 Ambient air temperature. +5 °C min. / +30 °C max.
5.4 Relative air humidity. 85% max.
5.5 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.7):
    - Do not mix and apply product that has a temperature of greater than 30oC. If applying at higher 30oC, as soon as the Sikagard®-62 T is mixed transfer the container into an esky containing ice to just below the rim of the container, then apply the Sikagard®-62 T from the open container in the esky.
    - The temperature at which the Sikagard®-62 T is stored during the 24 hours before it is mixed will govern its potlife when mixed.
    - If the temperature of a porous substrate (which includes the avast majority of concrete) is rising i.e. is in direct sunlight prior to late afternoon, the air in the pores and cracks is expanding and if a wet coating is placed over such a substrate the expanding air will blow bubbles in the coating and pervent the liquid coating penetrating the substrate pores and cracks etc. Prior to the coating reaching the gel phase the bubbles will burst and leave "pinholes in coating, whereas during the gel phase, the bubbles will be "frozen" into the cured coating. These bubbles will be a weak point in the coating as their wall thickness will be less than the applied film thickness on the substrate.
    - To avoid unslightly water spotting do not apply Sikagard®-62 T when ambient temperature will reach "dew point" before the coating has cured.
    - Similarly do not allow water to contact Sikagard®-62 T that is not even seven (7) days old at 20oC or older at lower temperatures since it will mark the coating.
5.6 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.7 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sikagard®-62 T, April 2023, Version 01.02, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/7/sikagard-62-t.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sikagard®-62T Part A, version 07/12/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/z/sds-sikagard-62tparta.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
